name: SVG Path Editor
blurb: edit a path node by node and trim needless decimals
intro: Parses a path's d attribute by the SVG path grammar, lists every node, and writes it back shorter: rounded to the decimals you choose, each segment relative or absolute (whichever is shorter), H/V shorthands, no repeated command letters. Drag a node in the drawing to move it.

inputs.label: Path data
inputs.placeholder: M10 10 L90 10 L50 80 Z  (or a whole <path d="..."/>)

inputs.label: Drop needless spaces and leading zeros
Write straight lines as H / V where possible
Scale
inputs.help: Uniform; applied after reading, before rounding.

examples.title: An exported 24 px alert icon with six decimals
Scale a 100-unit logo path down to a 24 px icon

usage: Give d as the path data string (or a whole <path> element), decimals as 0-4 or keep, mode as shortest, relative or absolute, and optional translate tx/ty and uniform scale. Returns the rewritten path (texts 'Path' and 'Element' with a fitted viewBox), characters before and after, bounding box, sampled length, the largest node shift rounding caused, and a node table; result.segments holds the absolute segments. Use it to shrink icon paths or check what precision a path can lose.
sources: W3C SVG 1.1 section 8.3 (path data grammar) and appendix F.6.5-F.6.6 (arc endpoint to centre conversion)
